records.mutation: recast contradictions as branch-eliminating deductions and ban selecting a candidate on plausibility instead of checked conditions
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent hint scored 0/8, with 3 of 8 truncating at the token cap; every rollout enumerated the divisor pairs of the displayed number, correctly noticed that a speaker's own value pins the partner within one reading, then treated the resulting contradiction as a broken problem and either looped re-deriving the same cases until truncation or selected the most compound-looking divisor purely because it 'fits the logic' without checking a single condition. The incumbent already names the label ambiguity but never tells the student that a contradiction eliminates one branch or assumption rather than the setup, and its ban on unverified guessing was too weak to stop plausibility-based selection, so I made both explicit and cut length to help transfer.

records.mutation: replace open-ended recheck rule with a verification budget: probe the simplest degenerate instance, stop after one confirmation, and let the symbolic derivation outrank a disagreeing numeric probe after a single recheck
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct in 5.7k-9.1k tokens; the lone failure derived the correct locus and even confirmed it on the easy real instance, then mis-evaluated a complex instance (a dropped sign when inverting a reciprocal), and because the incumbent only says to recheck that one line it re-audited the same sound derivation dozens of times and exhausted the 16384-token cap without stating a result. The incumbent already had a correct verification instinct but no stopping rule, so I bound the checking: probe the simplest degenerate instance where signs and reciprocals cannot bite, stop after one confirmation, and after a single recheck let the symbolic derivation outrank a disagreeing numeric probe.

records.mutation: add a two-sided containment guard (overlap cannot vanish when the apex lies inside the region) and reframe invariance as a proof that makes extra angle checks redundant
records.subagent_summary: Only three of eight rollouts scored. Two distinct failures appeared: one asserted the larger square could be rotated so the overlap vanished entirely and reported the plain sum of areas, which the incumbent's one-sided anti-containment warning actually encourages, and another reached the right overlap early but then talked itself out of it while re-testing rotations; three more never closed the reasoning block at all before the token cap. The revision therefore makes the wedge caution two-sided (a wedge whose apex sits inside a region must clip a positive share of it, so a zero-overlap conclusion is a red flag) and replaces the bare stop instruction with a logical reason to stop: an invariance argument is itself a proof, so additional angle checks are redundant rather than prudent.

records.mutation: anchor the per-tool cap at exactly d (forbid further differencing) and shorten the reusability/impossibility guidance for earlier commitment
records.subagent_summary: Only 2 of 8 fresh rollouts were correct. The dominant error, in 4 of 8, was reporting the number of available tools as the cap after asserting each item needs its own tool; two others mis-sized the per-tool root budget, one landing one above the degree and one one below it after taking an extra difference. The revision therefore states plainly that tools are reusable so their count is never the cap, pins the per-tool budget at exactly the degree in both directions, bans further differencing of the residual, and trims wording so the count is stated earlier.

records.mutation: make root screening concrete (substitute the number, not a remembered interval) and add a degenerate-outcome-means-wrong-root reversal rule
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct and all eight terminated normally under 12k tokens, so non-termination is no longer the failure mode; the single wrong rollout had both correct candidate roots in hand, wrongly declared one out of the domain by appealing to a remembered interval, kept the root that made the two new vertices coincide with the given ones, and then reported the resulting collapse as the value instead of treating it as a red flag. I therefore kept the incumbent's terse name-reduce-crosscheck spine and sharpened only its discard clause: screen roots by substituting the number into the original conditions and the stated domain, and read a degenerate or trivial outcome as evidence the other root was the right one.

records.mutation: reframe as one shared sample space of free 50/50 atoms reused across all parts, with an explicit no-mixed-count rule for later parts
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent gave 3/8; seven rollouts terminated normally at 9k-15k tokens and one hit the cap while relitigating, so length is secondary. Every failure got the free-choice denominator idea partly right but then abandoned it on the later part, either retreating to an asserted uniform 1/n or putting a permutation count over a branch count, and two also swapped in a different denominator (all moves, or n!) between parts. The revision therefore makes the free-choice atom set a single shared sample space that must be reused verbatim for every part, names the mixed-count division as the specific error, and keeps the symmetry warning and small-case calibration that transferred best.

records.mutation: require substitute-back verification of each small case and a third-visit cutoff before pattern commit
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling under the incumbent scored 2 of 8; both successes tabulated a few exactly solved small instances and committed to the signed factorial-style form, while all six failures ran to the token cap. The failures split into two observed modes: an unverified small case producing wrong table entries that then drove a bogus pattern, and endless oscillation over whether the running index or the exponent was the polynomial variable, with the same reduced system re-solved several times with different arithmetic. The revision therefore makes a one-time substitute-back check mandatory per small case, admits only verified entries into the table, forces an explicit index-versus-exponent declaration before any polynomial recast, and adds a third-visit cutoff so budget goes to committing the checked pattern.

records.mutation: keep the incumbent sentences verbatim and append an anti-rumination clause (settle the reading once, drive to a number early, one independent recheck instead of re-litigation)
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored reward 1 with clean stops at 2.7-6.9k completion tokens, so train_i remains saturated at 1.0 and every available point of J must come from transfer. The dominant observable pathology is rumination rather than error: traces contain 4-21 self-interrupting restarts and 21-92 repetitions of the same per-unit-versus-total question, plus 13-22 circlings of the same divisor argument, all after the correct route was already visible. Prior rounds established that altering the incumbent's opening sentences collapses train (0.25/0.5/0.375) while verbatim-preserving appends hold it at 1.0, so this round keeps them untouched and appends a purely behavioral, domain-neutral loop-breaker instead of restating scope or divisor content that earlier appends already covered.

records.mutation: lead with a general problem-triage opening (restate the ask, harvest free equations from special inputs, check for fixed points) and generalize the ansatz jargon to smallest-structured-family, keeping the centered antisymmetric recipe as the specialization
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts were correct and every one terminated cleanly well under the token cap (4.1k-8.2k completion tokens), so the incumbent has fully solved the budget-exhaustion and ansatz-mis-parameterization failures that dominated earlier rounds; there is no remaining training failure mode to target. With train saturated and the objective weighting transfer double, the revision keeps the proven centered-antisymmetric core but spends its opening tokens on generic triage jargon that applies before any commuting-map structure is recognized, since the incumbent's opening jargon only fires on that one narrow pattern.

records.mutation: pin the definition of one application up front, and make iteration the sole authority over structural period claims (naming the transpositions-imply-period-2 fallacy) with the count allowed to exceed the step count
records.subagent_summary: Only 1 of 8 rollouts scored and 6 of the 8 hit the 16384-token cap; the dominant mechanism was a structural assertion that the composite is a product of disjoint transpositions and therefore has period 2, which the student then defended even after its own row-by-row iteration visibly failed to return to the start, spending the remaining budget relitigating instead of trusting the trace. Two rollouts also built maps that were plainly non-bijective and read that as exotic structure, and several burned thousands of tokens re-arguing whether one application meant the entire listed sequence or a single step. The revision therefore pins the meaning of one application up front, makes iteration the sole authority whenever it contradicts a structural claim, names the transpositions-imply-period-2 fallacy in the words the failures used, and states that the count may far exceed the number of steps.
